Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.prefs

Class FileAssociations

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.prefs.FileAssociations
public final class FileAssociations extends Object
The desktop's file-type -> application associations: which application opens which kind of file (for example, the PDF Viewer opens .pdf).

An association maps a type key to a handler command. The type key is either an extension (ext:pdf) or a MIME type (mime:application/pdf); the handler command uses the same vocabulary as the start-menu descriptors, so it may name one of the desktop's own applications (java org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.pdfviewer.PdfViewer), a conventional Swing app (swingapp ...) or an external executable (evince). A handler may embed the token %f, expanded to the file being opened; when it is absent the path is appended as a final argument (see expand(String, Path)).

Values are persisted through LgPreferencesHelper (i.e. java.util.prefs), one preference key per association, so a command containing ; or = cannot corrupt the store. The instance is a lazily-created singleton (get()); reads hit the backing node each time so every caller sees the latest associations without an explicit reload.

Opener.open(Path) consults this model before falling back to xdg-open, so a configured association takes effect everywhere a file is opened (the file manager, the desktop folders, the dock stacks).

      public static String normalizeTypeKey(String raw)

    • bareExtension

      public static String bareExtension(String fileName)
      The bare, lower-case extension of a filename or path, without the leading dot, or null when there is none (a dotfile such as .bashrc has no extension). Pure so it can be unit-tested.

    • extensionKeyOf

      public static String extensionKeyOf(Path path)
      The extension type key of path, or null when it has none. A dotfile such as .bashrc has no extension (see bareExtension(java.lang.String)).

    • mimeTypeOf

      public static String mimeTypeOf(Path path)
      The MIME type of path: the OS content-type probe first, then the built-in extension fallback (so detection still works on a system with no MIME database, and headless). Null when unknown.

    • expand

      public static List<String> expand(String command, Path path)
      Expands a handler command into an argv vector for path. Each whitespace-separated token containing %f has it replaced by the absolute path (as its own argument, so spaces are safe); when no token contains %f the absolute path is appended as a final argument. A null/blank command yields an empty vector. Pure so it can be unit-tested.
